description: Compares AIC/BIC for linear vs step-function models of dust vs t_eff and M*. Addresses the OLS AIC limitation: linear regression cannot capture the AGB step-function relationship.

step_teff_agb.description: Step-function: dust ~ 1 + I(t_eff > 0.3 Gyr). AGB-motivated threshold.

step_mass_matched.description: Step-function: dust ~ 1 + I(M* > quantile). Mass-matched to same fraction above threshold as t_eff step.

polynomial_mass_z.description: Polynomial: dust ~ 1 + M* + z + M*×z (4 parameters, OLS baseline)

key_comparisons.note: Both step-function models have same k=2 parameters. Delta AIC/BIC directly measures which threshold (t_eff or M*) better organizes the dust distribution.

interpretation.main_finding: The mass-matched step-function M* model (AIC=-334.8) outperforms the step-function t_eff model (AIC=-341.9) by ΔAIC=-7.1, despite identical parameter counts (k=2). The best-fitting model overall is the polynomial M*×z baseline (AIC=-516.6, Akaike weight=1.0). Both step-function models are dominated by the polynomial baseline (ΔAIC=174.6 and 181.7 respectively).
interpretation.ols_limitation: OLS linear regression penalizes t_eff because the AGB threshold creates a non-linear (step-function) relationship. However, even with the step-function functional form, the mass-matched threshold achieves lower AIC. The dust ratio above/below the t_eff threshold is only 1.70×, indicating a weak step contrast in the UNCOVER z>8 sample.
interpretation.consistency_with_step110: Real-data dust ratio above/below t_eff threshold: 1.70x, compared against the step_110 threshold result.
interpretation.conclusion: The step-function t_eff model does not outperform the mass-matched step-function M* model on AIC (ΔAIC=-7.1) or BIC (ΔBIC=-7.1). The polynomial M*×z model dominates all competitors. The AGB step-function contrast (dust ratio 1.70×) is present but weak in the UNCOVER z>8 sample. The case for t_eff over M* rests on the rank-correlation and Steiger Z tests (step_136), not on the step-function AIC comparison.
